newsitem.title: ITALY: Tired-sounding Pope appeals for Albania.
newsitem.headline: Tired-sounding Pope appeals for Albania.

text.p: Pope John Paul, sounding weak and tired, appealed to the international community on Monday to help restore peace and order in Albania.
The 76-year-old Pope travelled to the Papal summer villa south of Rome for several days of rest following a hectic programme of Holy Week activities that culminated on Easter Sunday.
The Pope's voice seemed weak and tired and at times trembling as he addressed several thousand people in the courtyard of the villa.
The Pontiff, who has had a series of health problems in recent years, also appeared tired during Sunday's Easter mass at the Vatican.
The Pontiff told the pilgrims at Castel Gandolfo that the joy of Easter had been disturbed by the sinking of an Albanian refugee ship on Friday night.
Addressing them from a first-storey window of an internal courtyard, the Pope asked for prayers for the dead and for relatives who were suffering "tormenting pain" over their loss of loved ones.
He asked for a redoubling of efforts to bring Albania emergency aid "as well as social order and peace and collaboration to re-launch economic activity".
Albania needed help to get back on its feet and build its own future, he said.
Rome is preparing a multinational force to protect aid to the lawless country.
Tirana says around 80 refugees fleeing unrest may have died in the Adriatic on Friday night after their Russian-built vessel collided with an Italian navy ship.
The disaster overshadowed Rome's preparations to lead a U.N.-approved force of about 2,500 police or troops to protect deliveries of food and medicines to Albania, with another 2,500 in reserve.
